material: SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), as listed for FM2 in the 2024 FM2 poster

conditions.flow: quiescent (no forced flow; buoyant flow only); downward (opposed) spread

expectation.range: steady flame-base spread rate 0.6-1.4 mm/s (our interval around the LUCI value of 0.92 mm/s; it stays below the 1.5 mm/s LUCI 1-g ground value)

basis.claim: SIBAL burned downward in air at rotation-simulated lunar g with steady spread: flame base 0.92 mm/s, flame tip 1.1 mm/s
basis.source: Ferkul et al. 2025, LUCI presentation (ASGSR 2025), NTRS 20250010653

basis.claim: In the 1-g ground comparison the SIBAL flame went out about 45 s sooner than in partial g; linear-fit base/tip rates were 1.5/2.8 mm/s at 1 g versus 0.9/1.1 mm/s at partial g
basis.source: Ferkul et al. 2025, LUCI presentation (ASGSR 2025), NTRS 20250010653

basis.claim: SIBAL fabric 'has been found to only burn downward in air in lunar gravity (via Lunar gravity centrifuge and parabolic flight) where on Earth's gravity it extinguishes immediately after ignition'
basis.source: Zayac, Johnston, Ruff & Ferkul 2024, FM2 poster, NTRS 20240015307

basis.claim: FM2 plans two SIBAL samples burned in air (21% O2, 14.7 psia), one upward and one downward
basis.source: Zayac, Johnston, Ruff & Ferkul 2024, FM2 poster, NTRS 20240015307

confirmed_if: The FM2 downward SIBAL burn in air keeps a flame spreading for at least 30 s after the igniter turns off. The range part is confirmed if the reported steady base spread rate is between 0.6 and 1.4 mm/s.
refuted_if: The flame extinguishes within 10 s after the igniter turns off, or never establishes steady spread (direction refuted). The range part is refuted if the steady base spread rate is below 0.6 or above 1.4 mm/s.
caveats: LUCI used centrifugal gravity on a spinning rocket; Coriolis force deflected the flames (slide 17).
The nominal 0.165 g is our derivation from 11 RPM and 1.22 m (slide 12). The gravity traces plotted on slides 41 and 44 sit near 0.18 g. This is our visual reading of the plot.
LUCI is one test per material, with no replicates. Its pressure is stated only as 'normal pressure'.
The two 1-g sources disagree. The LUCI ground SIBAL burn spread before going out, while the 2024 poster says SIBAL extinguishes immediately at 1 g.
O2 fell from about 20% to 18% during the LUCI SIBAL burn (slide 42). FM2's chamber volume and sample size are not published.
The 30 s and 10 s thresholds and the rate interval are our choices, not NASA criteria.

material: Acrylic (PMMA). The 2024 FM2 poster lists two acrylic rods. This branch applies to any FM2 sample that is a thermoplastic or cellulosic material failing NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 in air.

conditions.flow: quiescent (buoyant only); upward and downward samples per the 2024 poster

expectation.range: extinction O2 (from chamber O2 depletion) lower than NASA's 1-g value from the same hardware and protocol. Our central guess is about 2 percentage points lower, based on the ICES-2025 conservative PMMA factor of 1.9.

basis.claim: At 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) the lunar-g centrifuge limit for 0.8 mm PMMA was lower than any extrapolation of the 1-g data. The conservative 1-g to lunar correction is 1.9 % O2.
Mylar G, a non-charring thermoplastic film: the midpoint of its burn (ULOI) and extinction (MOC) limits was 5.75 points lower in lunar gravity than at 1 g (70.3 kPa)
LUCI describes the chamber O2 drop during burning as 'enabling a limiting value for extinction to be defined'
basis.source: Ferkul et al. 2025, LUCI presentation (ASGSR 2025), NTRS 20250010653

basis.claim: FM2 can reproduce 21% O2 at 14.7 psia and 34% O2 at 8.2 psia; the two acrylic rods are planned for 'Normoxic Space Exploration Atmospheres (SEA)'
basis.source: Zayac, Johnston, Ruff & Ferkul 2024, FM2 poster, NTRS 20240015307

confirmed_if: FM2 reports, or allows us to compute, an extinction O2 for an acrylic sample in lunar gravity that is lower than NASA's 1-g reference value for the same configuration by more than the stated sensor uncertainty.
refuted_if: The lunar extinction O2 is equal to or higher than the 1-g reference value, within sensor uncertainty. The test is inconclusive if the sample burns out before O2 depletion causes extinction, or if no 1-g reference is published.
caveats: The 2024 poster does not state 34% O2 / 8.2 psia for the acrylic rods; we assume it because it is the only exploration atmosphere the poster names.
The ICES-2025 lunar values come from 5.2 s drop-tower centrifuge tests and are given only in figures. The 1.9 factor is an extrapolation, not a lunar measurement.
The Mylar shift (-5.75) was measured at 70.3 kPa with a 5.18 s criterion, not at 56.5 kPa. Its lunar point comes from Ferkul & Olson 2011, which we have not read.
In LUCI (air, about 101 kPa) the PMMA O2 traces ended at similar values in flight and on the ground (14.3% vs 14.5%; slides 22, 31). That weakens the expected magnitude.
In LUCI the gravity dropped from about 125 s during the PMMA burn (slides 22, 43; slide 44 plot), even though the slide 44 text says '~constant'.
Rod diameter and FM2 chamber volume are not published. At 34% O2 the sample may burn out before O2 depletion causes extinction.

material: Conditional branch: any FM2 sample that passes NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 in air and has a high pyrolysis temperature, such as Nomex or polycarbonate. This may include 'Synergy Pro', named for FM2 in the 2025 Nomex poster; its composition is not verified by us.

basis.claim: At 56.5 kPa, polycarbonate and Nomex Velcro extinguished in lunar g at 'substantially higher' O2 than the 1-g WSTF data
Nomex HT90-40 at 8.2 psi: approximate LOC ~23% at 1 g, ~29% at lunar g, ~38% at 0 g
basis.source: Schechter et al. 2025, Nomex/FM2 poster, NTRS 20250010975

basis.claim: FM2 'will determine limiting oxygen concentration (LOC) for a flight-relevant material (Synergy Pro)'
basis.source: Schechter et al. 2025, Nomex/FM2 poster, NTRS 20250010975

basis.claim: The Nomex HT-90 tests 'are designed to help guide the final selection of fuel, oxygen concentration, and ignition parameters for FM2'

confirmed_if: FM2 reports a lunar extinction O2 (or LOC) for such a material that is equal to or higher than the 1-g reference value for the same configuration.
refuted_if: The lunar extinction O2 is lower than the 1-g reference value by more than the sensor uncertainty.
caveats: The opposite direction was measured at 101.3 kPa: Nomex HT90-40 had its lunar O2 limit 2.35 points below 1 g (Olson & Ferkul 2012, Table I, p.6). The sign may depend on pressure.
The Nomex poster values are approximate (~) and include an unexplained note: '* Assuming a buoyant velocity of 25 cm/s'.
This branch applies only if FM2 flies such a material. The 2024 FM2 poster lists only SIBAL and acrylic.
